St. Louis Cardinals rookie outfielder Joshua Báez clobbered a home run 450 feet on the first pitch of his big league career. (This video contains AI-assisted content)

St. Louis Cardinals rookie Joshua Báez’s first career game in the big leagues was something out of a movie.

Báez made Major League Baseball history by hitting a home run in each of his first three plate appearances in the Cardinals' game against the Chicago Cubs on Saturday afternoon at Wrigley Field. The 23-year-old wasted no time in his first-ever at bat, as he blasted the first pitch he saw in his major league career 450 feet to dead center field for a two-run homer to give the Cardinals a 3-0 lead.

Báez pummeled Cubs starter Matt Boyd’s 93-mph fastball and sent the Cardinals’ dugout into a frenzy. The rookie rounded the bases with a smile on his face the entire time.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Joshua Báez of the St. Louis Cardinals hits a home run during the first inning against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field in Chicago, Ill., on Aug. 15, 2026. (Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images)

His second home run of the day came in the fourth inning, once again off Boyd. Báez worked the count full and then hammered Boyd's 78-mph changeup 382 feet into the left-field seats to give the Cardinals a 4-3 lead.

Báez's third home run also came off Boyd, this time off an 83-mph slider on the outside of the plate. The electrifying rookie hammered the ball 368 feet into the right-field seats for a two-run home run, giving the Cardinals a 6-3 lead. The Cardinals' dugout was in disbelief, with multiple players in awe of Báez's historic feat.

The right-handed hitter homered to all three fields on three different pitches in his first three plate appearances of his career. Báez homered off a fastball in his first at-bat to center field, a changeup to left field in his second at-bat, and a slider to right field in his third at-bat. It was a remarkable display of power in his first career game.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Joshua Báez No. 22 of the St. Louis Cardinals celebrates with Alec Burleson No. 41 after hitting a home run during the first inning against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field in Chicago, Ill., on Aug. 15, 2026. (Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images)

In his fourth at-bat, he proved he was human, as he just hit a line out to Cubs left fielder Ian Happ. At the time of this writing, the Cardinals had an 8-4 lead over the Cubs in the ninth inning.

Báez, who led Triple-A in home runs before being called up on Saturday, was batting fifth in the order and playing left field. In Triple-A, the Boston native was putting up massive numbers, hitting .256 with 34 home runs, 90 RBI and 21 stolen bases in 103 games.

The Cardinals drafted him in the second round of the 2021 MLB Draft out of high school. The team hopes he can join JJ Wetherholt, Jordan Walker and Alec Burleson to form a young core the team can build around for a long time.

Joshua Báez of the St. Louis Cardinals celebrates after hitting a home run during the first inning against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field in Chicago, Ill., on Aug. 15, 2026. (Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images)

The Cardinals were not expected to compete this season but have surprised many as they entered Saturday at 61-61 and just 3.5 games back of the Arizona Diamondbacks and Philadelphia Phillies for the final Wild Card spot in the National League.

articles.title: Qatar denies Tehran’s claim it is detaining Iranian bomber pilots
articles.excerpt:
Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has denied Tehran’s claims that Iranian pilots are being held in secret detention following the downing of their aircraft during hostilities earlier this year.

A m...
articles.body_text:
Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has denied Tehran’s claims that Iranian pilots are being held in secret detention following the downing of their aircraft during hostilities earlier this year.

A ministry spokesman expressed surprise on Saturday at “misleading statements” from Iranian officials and reaffirmed that Qatari forces are not holding any surviving aircrew.

“We categorically deny the claims circulating regarding the detention of Iranian pilots & are surprised by these misleading statements at this particular time, amid the ongoing diplomatic efforts & initiatives aimed at de-escalating tensions in the region,” said Qatar’s Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari in a post on X.

His statement followed public demands from Tehran seeking the release of the aviators. General Mohammad Bagherzadeh of the Iranian armed forces said in a letter to the International Committee of the Red Cross that three pilots, Javad Salehi, Abdolmajid Dashtian and Omran Behraveshian, were captured alive after their Su-24 warplanes crashed in March, according to Iran’s Fars news agency.

Bagherzadeh stated that the airmen had been held incommunicado for six months without access to their families or diplomatic representatives, urging international humanitarian intervention.

Iran had previously acknowledged that one pilot was killed and the others were missing following their mission to Qatar, but details regarding their alleged capture had not previously been publicised.

Doha confirmed that Qatari air defence forces established contact with the aircraft after an unauthorised breach of Qatari airspace in March. After receiving no response to warnings, Qatari forces engaged the targets. Search and rescue teams later recovered the remains of one pilot, Majid Kazemi, and coordinated with Iranian authorities for the repatriation of his body.

“Qatar … communicated with the Iranian side to coordinate the handover of the remains of one of the pilots who was found, in accordance with the relevant provisions of international humanitarian law,” al-Ansari said on Saturday. “Qatar also issued an invitation for an Iranian team to visit Qatar to be briefed on the details of the search & rescue operations in April, but the Iranian side has yet to respond to the invitation.”

The military engagement came during an attack onthe  Al Udeid airbase in Qatar, the largest United States military installation in the region, which hosts US Central Command (CENTCOM) personnel. In early March, Qatar’s Defence Ministry reported shooting down two Iranian Sukhoi Su-24 bombers, marking the first time a Gulf country reported downing Iranian aircraft during the conflict.

The interception came amid the broader wave of retaliatory strikes across the Gulf following the outbreak of hostilities on February 28. Although an April ceasefire brokered alongside initial mediator Pakistan temporarily halted major combat, peace framework talks collapsed in June. That led to sporadic clashes near the Strait of Hormuz and renewed attacks on regional shipping and infrastructure.

Despite this dispute, Qatar remains actively engaged as a key mediator and is pushing for a negotiated settlement between Iran and the US.

The diplomatic friction comes as broader peace efforts face difficulties ahead of a key deadline. A 60-day negotiating window established under a mid-June memorandum of understanding expires on Monday, with few direct talks having happened, leaving maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz at a trickle.

Addressing an audience on Friday in New York, US President Donald Trump said Iran was being “very badly defeated” and suggested he would “pretty soon be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States”.

Tehran swiftly rejected the remarks on Saturday.

Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi posted on X that the strategically vital waterway “cannot be seized with a tweet, nor with an aircraft carrier”, warning that Iran would continue to enforce its blockade until Washington accepts “the reality of defeat”.

articles.title: Trump backs Republican challenger to oust Letitia James amid ongoing mortgage fraud feud
articles.excerpt:
New York Attorney General candidate Saritha Komatireddy explains why she is the right person to fix crime issues in New York and discusses public safety in the Mamdani era on ‘The Story.’

New York At...
articles.body_text:
New York Attorney General candidate Saritha Komatireddy explains why she is the right person to fix crime issues in New York and discusses public safety in the Mamdani era on ‘The Story.’

New York Attorney General Letitia James has drawn a Trump-backed challenger, with President Donald Trump throwing his "complete and total endorsement" behind Republican Saritha Komatireddy in a bid to oust his longtime political foe.

"It is my Great Honor to endorse America First Patriot, Saritha Komatireddy, who is running to be the next Attorney General of the once wonderful State of New York," Trump wrote in a Friday Truth Social post. "Between Kathy Hochul and the Most Corrupt Attorney General in the Country, Letitia James, it has gone to HELL!"

Trump’s endorsement of Komatireddy, who he nominated to U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York in 2020, comes as he continues pressing for James to be prosecuted over mortgage fraud allegations, adding another front to his years-long feud with the Democratic attorney general who once took him to court.

President Donald Trump endorsed Saritha Komatireddy in the New York attorney general's race to unseat foe Letitia James ((Photo by Jim WATSON / AFP via Getty Images) (Photo by Kena Betancur / AFP) (Photo by KENA BETANCUR/AFP via Getty Images))

TRUMP'S JUSTICE DEPARTMENT SUES NEW YORK, OTHER BLUE STATES OVER TUITION FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS

Trump did not mince his words in his criticism of James, who successfully sued Trump and The Trump Organization in 2022, accusing them of fraudulently inflating the value of assets on financial statements to obtain more favorable loans.

An appeals court later wiped out the nearly $465 million financial penalty against Trump, ruling the massive disgorgement award violated the Constitution’s prohibition on excessive fines.

"Letitia 'Peekaboo' James, is considered by many to be the WORST Attorney General in our Country. She is a Complete and Total Disaster, who tried running against Kathy Hochul for Governor, and got less than 1% of the Vote in the Polls, and QUIT, taking many innocent suckers down with her," Trump wrote. "She then went back to her WITCH HUNT against your favorite President, (ME!), and others, yet Murder and other Violent Crime is RAGING OUT OF CONTROL in New York, as People and Businesses flee, in Record Numbers, to other States!"

New York Attorney General Letitia James attends a campaign rally with community leaders in the Jackson Heights neighborhood in the Queens borough of New York City on Nov. 1, 2022. (AP Photo/Eduardo Munoz Alvarez, File)

He contrasted James to Komatireddy, touting her qualifications as Drug Enforcement Administration chief of staff, a former federal prosecutor, and that she clerked for Brett Kavanaugh, who went on to become a Supreme Court justice.

"On the other hand, as your next Attorney General, Saritha Komatireddy will fight tirelessly to Ensure LAW AND ORDER, Grow our Economy, Champion our Law Enforcement and First Responders, Support our Military/Veterans, Advance Election Integrity, Keep our Border SECURE, Stop Migrant Crime, Uphold our Constitution, and Defend our always under siege Second Amendment," Trump wrote.

Republican candidate for New York Attorney General Saritha Komatireddy holds a news conference with state GOP lawmakers on increasing public transit safety in New York on Wednesday, April 29, 2026, at West Capitol Park in Albany, N.Y. (Will Waldron/Albany Times Union via Getty Images))

TRUMP MAY HAVE ENDORSED DARLINE GRAHAM, BUT GOP SENATE HOPEFULS AREN’T BACKING DOWN

Komatireddy, who has been outspoken against James' handling of the state's fraud investigations, thanked Trump for his endorsement.

"I was honored to be nominated to be a federal judge by the President in 2020 and I’m honored to receive his endorsement today. I’m working hard to win the support of all New Yorkers and defeat Letitia James this November," Komatireddy wrote on X.

Fox News Digital reached out to James' campaign for comment.

Elaine Mallon is a writer for Fox News Digital and Fox Business covering national politics.

articles.title: California tackles multiple wildfires as firefighter workforce faces strain
articles.excerpt:
Firefighters in the western United States and Canada are working to contain multiple wildfires, including one that erupted along California’s rugged Big Sur coastline.

The state’s wildland firefighti...
articles.body_text:
Firefighters in the western United States and Canada are working to contain multiple wildfires, including one that erupted along California’s rugged Big Sur coastline.

The state’s wildland firefighting agency Cal Fire said in an update on Saturday that the Big Sur blaze, nicknamed the Timber Fire, is currently burning across 4,655 acres (1,884 hectares). Only 12 percent of the fire is contained so far.

Officials have indicated that hot, dry weather across the western part of North America has helped to fuel the blazes, displacing thousands of residents.

With the Timber Fire, Cal Fire noted the wind also presents a factor in the outdoor conditions.

“Any morning clouds along ridges and east of the fire should erode quickly with winds increasing in the afternoon,” Saturday’s update reads. “A warming and drying trend is predicted through the weekend and into next week.”

State parks in the area have been closed, and authorities have issued evacuation orders for portions of Highway 1, a famous road that traces the California coast, attracting visitors from around the world.

The Big Sur section of Highway 1 offers some of the state’s most stunning views, with sheer drops into the sea and a 24-metre (79-foot) waterfall tumbling from a cliff to the beach below.

Across the state, on the border between California and Nevada, firefighters are also working to contain the fast-moving Bug Fire near the city of Reno. So far, it has consumed about 93,381 acres (37,790 hectares) and is 58 percent contained, according to Cal Fire.

Washoe County Sheriff Darin Balaam stated in a news conference earlier this week that the fire had prompted the displacement of at least 4,000 people, including the evacuation of a memory care facility.

Firefighters are facing increasing strain in recent years as the blazes they battle have grown larger and more destructive due to climate change.

Shifting politics have also had an effect on the federal firefighting workforce.

The National Federation of Federal Employees (NFFE), a labour union, said in a statement on Friday that budget cuts and layoffs imposed under President Donald Trump have heaped uncertainty onto the beleaguered workforce.

The union referenced the actions undertaken by the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), an initiative Trump pursued during his second term to slash the federal government.

“In the middle of fire season, DOGE and the Trump administration’s policies and actions have weakened our ability to safely fight wildfires,” NFFE National President Randy Erwin said.

“DOGE recklessly cut more than 6,000 [US Forest Service] workers, thousands of them qualified wildland firefighters, and the Trump administration now threatens pointless relocations or terminations of many more, including shuttering 57 of 77 research labs critical to fire preparedness and response.”

While working conditions among firefighters can vary widely by agency and status, advocates say federal wildland firefighters have long faced poor pay and benefits, compounding the stress of their often life-threatening jobs.

articles.title: Mets' Jefry Yan, known for high-flying strikeout celebration, performs it too soon in hilarious blunder
articles.excerpt:
Former major league pitcher Collin Balester discusses his take on Mets pitcher Jefry Yan's wild strikeout celebration that has been raising eyebrows around baseball.

New York Mets fans can’t get enou...
articles.body_text:
Former major league pitcher Collin Balester discusses his take on Mets pitcher Jefry Yan's wild strikeout celebration that has been raising eyebrows around baseball.

New York Mets fans can’t get enough of Jefry Yan’s acrobatic celebration when he strikes out a batter in relief, as it’s become quite the social media sensation.

But Yan got too excited on Saturday afternoon in the Mets’ thrilling walk-off win over the Washington Nationals at Citi Field when he performed the viral celebration.

The pitch hadn’t been called strike three.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Jefry Yan of the New York Mets reacts after the ninth inning against the Washington Nationals at Citi Field on Aug. 15, 2026. (Getty Images)

Yan made his Citi Field debut in front of the Mets faithful, and in the top of the ninth with an 0-2 count and two out, he thought he placed his fastball perfectly on the outside corner to strike out Nasim Nuñez to end the frame.

The home plate umpire thought otherwise, but Yan was already midair in celebration. Yan, who seems to have springs in his feet with the way he jumps into the air to start his celebration, noticed that strike three wasn’t called.

As he touched back down on the mound, he started tapping the top of his hat to challenge the ball, forcing an ABS review.

ANTHONY VOLPE HAS FACE-PALM MOMENT WITH ABS SYSTEM AS FIRST BATTER OF MINOR LEAGUE GAME

But, after review, the umpire’s call for a ball stood.

"Now, that was funny," Mets longtime play-by-play announcer Gary Cohen said on the SNY broadcast.

After everyone got their laughs out, Yan made sure the celebration didn’t come back to haunt him. Two pitches later, he got Nuñez to strike out on a slider. This time, the celebration was worth it.

At the time of the strikeout, the Mets were down by a run heading into the bottom of the ninth inning. They needed to muster at least one run to force extra innings, but the offense wanted to end the game in their favor instead.

Jefry Yan of the New York Mets reacts after striking out a Washington Nationals batter to end the eighth inning at Citi Field on Aug. 15, 2026. (Getty Images)

Brett Baty walked to begin the inning and things got very interesting when Jorge Polanco singled to put the winning run on base. Then, Francisco Alvarez roped a double to left, tying the game as Baty came across the plate with the winning run moving to third base.

Francisco Lindor would start a celebration for everyone at Citi Field, especially Yan and the rest of his Mets teammates, when he singled home the winning run to walk it off in the ninth.

In doing so, Yan earned his first career win in MLB after pitching a scoreless 1.2 innings for the Mets.

Yan, a 29-year-old rookie, has had quite the year, which began in the minors. That’s where the baseball world learned of his unique celebration after getting strikeouts, and the big leagues have seen it now over his first five appearances for New York.

But whenever Yan wants to jump and tap the ground to celebrate, perhaps he’ll make certain the umpire has rung up the hitter before doing so.

Then again, he was really hoping to do it with Mets fans in the stands on his home field.

Jefry Yan of the New York Mets celebrates after striking out Angel Martínez of the Cleveland Guardians for his first career strikeout during his major league debut at Progressive Field on Aug. 5, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. (Getty Images)

"I felt really welcome today," Yan said through a translator about his first Citi Field appearance.

Yan, who struck out three hitters in his outing on Saturday, owns a 1.80 ERA thus far.

Follow Fox News Digital’s sports coverage on X and subscribe to the Fox News Sports Huddle newsletter.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: At least five reported dead amid flooding in US state of Indiana
articles.excerpt:
Authorities in the Midwestern United States have reported at least five deaths in Indiana after the state was struck with fierce storms and flooding.

Rescue workers continue to seek out those strande...
articles.body_text:
Authorities in the Midwestern United States have reported at least five deaths in Indiana after the state was struck with fierce storms and flooding.

Rescue workers continue to seek out those stranded by the storms, which drenched Indiana over the past week.

Governor Mike Braun had called for a presidential emergency declaration on Friday, in order to access greater resources for the state.

On Saturday, he issued a public statement announcing that the federal government had pledged assistance.

“I spoke with President [Donald] Trump today about the severe storms and historic flooding impacting Indiana, and he informed me that he intends to approve our request for a Presidential Emergency Declaration,” Braun, a Republican, wrote in a social media post.

“I’m grateful to President Trump for his commitment to getting Hoosiers the federal assistance we need as we continue responding and recovering.”

Emergency workers have used boats to rescue people from homes inundated by rising waters.

The White River in Indianapolis, Indiana, was among the waterways that overflowed its banks over the last week, causing dangerous flooding.

Indianapolis Mayor Joe Hogsett said that the area is experiencing its worst flooding in more than 30 years. The National Weather Service has reported that more than 280mm (11 inches) of rain fell over two days in some areas.

Sheriff deputies in Delaware County said on Friday that they had found the body of a deceased 58-year-old woman, whom they believe died trying to drive her vehicle through floodwaters.

Authorities caution against attempting to cross flooded areas in a car, warning that vehicles can become stranded.

A four-year-old child also died after a tree fell on a home in Jennings County this week, and law enforcement found the body of a teen who was reported missing on Wednesday after jumping into a river.

“My heart is with the families and loved ones of the five Hoosiers we have lost and every family whose life has been changed by these storms,” Braun said on Saturday. “Please continue to take flooding seriously and stay away from floodwaters.”

articles.title: Jaxson Dart gets last laugh against blitzing Vikings coach Brian Flores and the ominous blue medical tent
articles.excerpt: Nick Wright, Danny Parkins, Kevin Wildes and Coach Eric Mangini discuss whether Jaxson Dart is the next young star QB or not, then react to Josh Allen still feeling guilty over Sean McDermott's firing...
articles.body_text:
Nick Wright, Danny Parkins, Kevin Wildes and Coach Eric Mangini discuss whether Jaxson Dart is the next young star QB or not, then react to Josh Allen still feeling guilty over Sean McDermott's firing. They also discuss Patrick Mahomes' expectations coming off his injury. (00:00) Intro
(00:30) Jaxson Dart the Next Star?
(05:56) Josh Allen Still Feels Guilty Over McDermott
(15:07) Expectations for Patrick Mahomes

It was ugly when Jaxson Dart got absolutely rocked so hard during Saturday's preseason game that he lay motionless on the field as team trainers and doctors rushed to his aid.

The moment looked like a snapshot from the 2025 season, when the New York Giants' quarterback was hit over and over again. And, like a handful of times in 2025, this hit resulted in Dart being evaluated for a concussion out of concern for the player's safety.

Dart had one confirmed concussion out of those five previous evaluations and missed two games as a result.

ANTHONY RICHARDSON'S TURNOVERS IN PRESEASON OPENER RAISE MORE QUESTIONS ABOUT HIS COLTS FUTURE

New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is sacked during a preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings on Saturday, Aug. 15, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

"I never thought I was going to be taken out," Dart said after the game. "I want to keep playing until they tell me I'm not playing. Like, I want to be out there."

The Giants season flashed before everyone's eyes until Dart emerged from the blue medical tent on the sideline after the evaluation that cleared him to return.

But the whole scene raises questions about what should and shouldn't be expected in any team's first preseason game.

SUPREME COURT HANDS NFL A LOSS IN BRIAN FLORES DISCRIMINATION LAWSUIT, CLEARING PATH TO TRIAL

New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh speaks at the press conference announcing his hiring at Quest Diagnostics Training Center. (Ed Mulholland/Imagn Images)

Harbaugh said he had no hesitation about putting Dart back in the game and the quarterback told him he simply had the wind knocked out of him.

Harbaugh also said he was "honestly" surprised Dart was sent to the blue tent in the first place, but the job of doctors is to "err on the side of player safety."

(Yes, especially when a sizable part of Dart's rookie season felt like one long medical evaluation.)

We don't know why the Vikings blitzed as many times and ways as they did this game. Flores is known for doing this. It's his professional personality, one might argue.

Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores looks on during the fourth quarter of a game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on Jan. 4, 2026. (Matt Blewett/Imagn Images)

And, no, professional football leaves no room for mercy from a defensive unit and its coaches toward an opposing offense, its quarterback or its coaches.

It was the running back Tyrone Tracy's job to pick up the blitz by Ward.

Harbaugh, in fact, said his reaction to seeing his starting quarterback practically knocked into next week on the safety blitz was simple: "My feeling in that moment was we need to block better."

"Preseason football, you just don't expect all these looks your first game out," Giants analyst Phil Simms said on the broadcast.

And Flores, who unleashed those looks, is no fan of the Giants — or the Miami Dolphins, Houston Texans, Denver Broncos, Stephen Ross or John Elway, all of whom he named as defendants in his 2022 racial discrimination lawsuit.

That suit, by the way, is ongoing four years later, so Flores is still pressing the issue.

And it doesn't stretch credibility to think he might have wanted to make things difficult for the Giants based on the feelings he outlined in that suit.

The Giants, you may recall, presented perhaps the most vocal pushback against Flores when he claimed they discriminated against him when Brian Daboll was hired. Flores claimed the club used him for purposes of a sham Rooney Rule interview when it was already decided Daboll would get the job.

The Giants offered an unequivocal denial, saying the claims Flores made were "disturbing and simply false."

New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart scrambles during the fourth quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J., on Jan. 4, 2026. (Vincent Carchietta/Imagn Images)

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

So it wouldn't be surprising if Flores were still holding on to some resentment, given that he's a prideful person who might want to remind the Giants that he hasn't forgotten.

Flores did not speak to reporters after the game, per NFL guidelines.

Ultimately, it is up to Dart to recognize where rushers are coming from, be aware of his protection, see if it's breaking down, and get rid of the football. He took a lot of criticism about that as a rookie when he was hit 146 times by some counts in 12 starts.

But you know what? Dart ultimately got his measure of revenge this game.

He returned to the game and threw a 15-yard touchdown pass against the Vikings and their defensive coordinator. But even then he seemed to train his ire at the fact he had to have an evaluation.

"As far as the blue tent, I really respect the rules and the thought the NFL has behind keeping players healthy and reviewing things," Dart said. "But at the same time I'm still puzzled by — just feeling like every time that I get hit I find my way in there, which at times I still try to wrap my head around."

FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

articles.title: Colombia asks Trump to suspend tariffs as country reels from earthquake
articles.excerpt: Colombia’s new president has called on United States President Donald Trump to suspend tariffs targeting the South American country, which is reeling from a deadly earthquake that has killed hundreds....
articles.body_text:
Colombia’s new president has called on United States President Donald Trump to suspend tariffs targeting the South American country, which is reeling from a deadly earthquake that has killed hundreds.

President Abelardo de la Espriella said Saturday that he had requested the US “temporarily suspend” tariffs on Colombia to give “relief” to business owners.

On Monday, a 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck Colombia, killing at least 294 people and damaging or destroying tens of thousands of buildings across the country, according to Colombia’s National Unit for Disaster Risk Management.

US tariffs on Colombian products rose from 10 percent to 12.5 percent in late July, with a few exceptions including coffee and oil. The US is Colombia’s top export market.

The Colombian leader described his 10-minute conversation with President Trump as “very friendly and cordial”.

“I told him that we have a huge challenge ahead: rebuilding Colombia amid the extremely difficult and apocalyptic economic situation that I inherited,” de la Espriella said.

Colombia’s Finance Minister Miguel Gomez said the government was not yet considering raising taxes to find the approximately $6.4bn needed for reconstruction, local media have reported.

Shortly after a legal defeat on “Liberation Day” tariffs, the White House announced renewed tariffs targeting nearly every US trading partner, including Colombia, based on what it said were failures to uphold anti-forced labour measures.

Trump endorsed the right-wing de la Espriella, a millionaire lawyer-turned-politician, during his run for the presidency that culminated in a close victory over leftist Ivan Cepeda in June.

Since taking office in early August, de la Espriella has joined the so-called “Shield of the Americas”, an anti-cartel alliance headed by Trump and involving multiple South American nations.

The new Colombian president has also said he plans to forge a military alliance with the US and Israel to help bolster the country’s long-running conflict with armed groups.

articles.title: Henry Winkler opens up about the unexpected career he considered before becoming an actor
articles.excerpt:
Henry Winkler says he formed a friendship with Adam Sandler after he called to thank him for including him in his 'Chanukah Song.’

Henry Winkler is opening up about what career path he would have cho...
articles.body_text:
Henry Winkler says he formed a friendship with Adam Sandler after he called to thank him for including him in his 'Chanukah Song.’

Henry Winkler is opening up about what career path he would have chosen had he not gotten into acting.

During a recent interview on the "You Could Make This Beautiful" podcast, the 80-year-old actor shared that he almost decided to become a child psychologist, because he was so dyslexic that "whatever I could do, with the least amount of education" was what he wanted to do.

"I understand children. I’m able to listen, I think, to children. I’m interested in what they have to say and how they are. I marvel at their prowess in the universe," Winkler said. "Yes, I would work with children."

Ultimately, the actor found fame playing Arthur "Fonzie" Fonzarelli on "Happy Days" from 1974 to 1984, a role which earned him three Emmy Award nominations.

Winkler shared he thought about becoming a child psychologist before going into acting. (Olivia Wong/WireImage)

'HAPPY DAYS' STAR HENRY WINKLER FILMED HIS FIRST-EVER NUDE SCENE AT 79

The actor has spoken about his lifelong struggle with dyslexia many times in the past and about how he learned to manage it in his career.

"Destiny is very strange, because I've chosen a profession that is so unbelievably difficult, not only to survive in, but to participate in for me," he told "PBS News Weekend" in November 2023. "When we were doing 'Happy Days' or any table read, which is the whole cast all the producers, the directors, everybody on the crew listening, for the first time to the script. I couldn't read off the page. And it was embarrassing. It was humiliating. I covered it with humor."

To manage the obstacles dyslexia presented in his career, Winkler explained that he would "literally read one word at a time" and ask for the script to be delivered to him ahead of time so that he would "almost memorize it" so that by the time it came to the table read, "I could read it with a flow."

While the actor had struggled with dyslexia his whole life, he didn't receive a diagnosis until he was in he was 31, and his young stepson was diagnosed with it, telling PBS that he was initially angry after getting a diagnosis.

Winkler didn't receive a dyslexia diagnosis until he was in his 30s, when his stepson was diagnosed. (MEGA/GC Images)

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I was because I was humiliated. I was constantly browbeaten. I was punished, grounded for most of my life," he said. "Then the next stage was all right, so I have this thing. Now I have to learn to negotiate it because it doesn't go away. It is the wiring in your brain."

He later learned to reframe the situation and began thinking, "maybe I would not be sitting in this chair" if he hadn't gone through "the challenge to constantly work through that made my tenacity, like steel."

Following his time on "Happy Days," Winkler continued acting, introducing himself to a younger audience in the 1998 movie, "The Waterboy," alongside Adam Sandler.

He then appeared in TV shows such as "Arrested Development," "Parks and Recreation" and "New Girl," before landing a starring role in the hit HBO Max show, "Barry," playing Gene Cousineau, an acting coach who finds himself befriending an assassin.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Winkler won his first Emmy Award in 2018 for his role in the HBO Max show, "Barry." (Neilson Barnard/FilmMagic)

The role earned him his first ever Emmy Award win in 2018.

"Be yourself, be honest about your ability, prepare so that you are not a flash in the pan," he said backstage after his win, per Variety.

"When I first started here in Hollywood … I thought of myself as a tree or sapling. I planted. I wanted to grow and be strong until I couldn’t do this anymore. And what a great tree it is."

Lori A. Bashian is an entertainment news writer at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: US Democrats finalise major shakeup to 2028 presidential primary calendar
articles.excerpt:
Democrats in the United States have approved a shakeup to their 2028 presidential primary calendar as the party looks to take back the White House.

During a meeting on Saturday in Austin, Texas, Demo...
articles.body_text:
Democrats in the United States have approved a shakeup to their 2028 presidential primary calendar as the party looks to take back the White House.

During a meeting on Saturday in Austin, Texas, Democratic National Committee (DNC) members voted to overhaul which states have the first say in picking the party’s presidential nominee.

South Carolina will once again take centre stage as the party’s first official nominating contest, with its Democratic primary scheduled for January 22, 2028.

Nevada will go second on February 1, followed by New Hampshire on February 8. New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia will round out the early states over the course of that month.

The new calendar formalises a change that began during the last presidential election cycle in 2024, when the national Democratic Party similarly put South Carolina at the front of its primary lineup.

The 2028 primaries set up a more competitive calendar for Democrats, giving greater influence to states with more racial diversity, in an effort to better represent the party’s key constituencies.

But plans to reshape the primary calendar have been met with controversy in the past.

In 2024, for instance, local leaders in New Hampshire defied party leaders by holding a state-run primary ahead of the first party-led vote in South Carolina. As justification, New Hampshire officials cited a state law requiring their primary to be the first in the nation.

There was also pushback in Iowa, whose state caucus had ushered in the primary season for decades.

Iowa Democrats warned that moving the state lower in the party’s calendar could send the wrong signal to rural voters, who often feel overlooked in national politics and tend to lean rightward.

Still, proponents of the calendar change argue that it will help the Democratic primaries better mirror the overall population of the US.

South Carolina has normally been Democrats’ first contest in the southern US, and it has a significant population of Black voters. Roughly a quarter of the state identifies as Black, according to census estimates.

Nevada and New Mexico, meanwhile, have large Latino or Hispanic populations, with 31 percent and 49 percent of their residents identifying as such, respectively. All three states will be at the forefront of the primary calendar, come 2028.

DNC Chairman Ken Martin took to social media on Saturday to tout the changes as capturing the demographic shifts in the country.

“These states reflect the diversity of America and will help ensure our nominee is best positioned to take back the White House in 2028,” Martin wrote on X.

Iowa and New Hampshire both have overwhelmingly white electorates, and critics have long argued the two states have played outsized roles in shaping presidential elections.

Notching early victories in the party primaries can help a candidate build momentum, and that, in turn, can help presidential hopefuls secure party nominations.

Former Vermont Governor Howard Dean, who led the DNC from 2005 to 2009, told The Associated Press (AP) news agency that the calendar changes will make for a more representative nominating process.

“These states look more like the country,” Dean said, pointing to places like South Carolina and Nevada, “whereas Iowa and New Hampshire don’t”.

But it remains uncertain how the new calendar could affect the growing intra-party feud between progressive and more moderate, establishment candidates.

Democrats in Michigan, one of the states given a boost in the calendar shakeup, narrowly voted earlier this month to select progressive Abdul El-Sayed as their Senate nominee.

Given that Michigan will now have an earlier say in the voting process, some experts have speculated that the swing state could help progressives assert greater influence over the party overall.

But other states given more prominence in the 2028 lineup have a more moderate streak.

South Carolina, for instance, favoured then-candidate Joe Biden in the 2020 primaries over his more progressive opponents, Senators Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren.

“I think our primary voters up north are probably a little different than primary voters in South Carolina,” Boyd Brown, a former DNC member from South Carolina, told AP.

articles.title: Roger Miller given stark choice after getting caught stealing: ‘You can go to jail or you can go in the Army’
articles.excerpt:
Country music star Lee Greenwood discusses the re-launch of his distillery, Soldier Valley Spirits, ahead of America's 250th birthday on 'America Reports.'

Roger Miller's son is getting candid about ...
articles.body_text:
Country music star Lee Greenwood discusses the re-launch of his distillery, Soldier Valley Spirits, ahead of America's 250th birthday on 'America Reports.'

Roger Miller's son is getting candid about why his famous father joined the Army as a teenager.

During a recent interview on the "Drifting Cowboy" podcast, the country music legend's son, Dean Miller, discussed how his father grew up "on a farm with no electricity" and would spend the weekends driving to Amarillo, Texas to play shows at a nightclub in an effort to break into the music industry.

"He would play at this one club, and he was friends with the guy and my dad, as he describes it, was ignorant and didn't know how to break into show business or how to get out of town or what to do with his life," he said.

Dean explained that his dad later had the idea that "if he stole a bunch of stuff from this club, he'd have all he needed to be in show business," leading him to steal equipment and costumes. According to the singer's website, he stole a guitar because he wanted it "so desperately to write songs," and turned himself in the next day.

The country singer's son recalled how his father ended up in the Army. (Silver Screen Collection/Hulton Archive/Getty Images)

"The police caught him and the guy that he stole from wrote a letter to the judge and said, 'Please be lenient on this kid. He doesn't know any better. He's a good kid."' And all this stuff," Dean said. "And so they told my dad, 'You can go to jail or you can go in the Army. Your choice.' And he chose the Army."

After joining the Army, Roger was deployed to Korea during the Korean War, which he referred to as the "Korea Clash of '52."

Dean recalled his father telling him that while in Korea, "I just spent the whole time hiding under a jeep and crying."

Ultimately, his time in the Army helped him in his music career, with Dean saying that is where "he met people in music" and was able to get "recommendations to people back home and started coming to Nashville after that."

Miller won 11 Grammy Awards in two years, and was nominated for a total of 18. (Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

It was while he was in the Army that he met his longtime friend and writing partner, Bill Anderson. The two would go on to write many hit songs together, including "When Two Worlds Collide," which became a Top 10 hit.

Roger is often regarded as a major figure in country music, credited for broadening the range of the genre by including elements of pop music in his songs.

Between 1965 and 1966, Roger won 11 Grammy Awards, including best contemporary country album for "Dang Me/Chug-A-Lug," and best country song for "Dang Me" and "King of the Road." He received a total of 18 nominations.

Throughout his career, he also wrote the score for the Broadway musical, "Big River," and the soundtrack for the Disney movie, "Robin Hood." He was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1995, three years after his death.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Kacey Musgraves called Roger Miller an icon. (Timothy Norris)

"Look at Buck Owens or Roger Miller; they're both icons in my eyes," Kacey Musgraves told The Boot in 2018. "Roger Miller was known for his humor, but there was a lot of deep water under those songs, and a lot of meat on those bones. Look at all the places he went: From Broadway to Disney. To me, if you look beyond the box, the whole world is waiting — no matter what you call the music, just be true to what you're doing."

The country music icon died in October 1992 at the age of 56 following a battle with lung cancer.

Lori A. Bashian is an entertainment news writer at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Ex-detective who served fraction of 102-year sentence faces new charges after cold case review
articles.excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on Foxnews.com.

A former Los Angeles vice detective who was sentenced to 102 years in prison three decades ago for multiple rapes but ...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on Foxnews.com.

A former Los Angeles vice detective who was sentenced to 102 years in prison three decades ago for multiple rapes but paroled in 2020, because of a California law was arrested again this week, authorities said.

Michael Douglas Brambles, 77, is charged with kidnapping to commit robbery while personally using a firearm in connection with an alleged robbery and sexual assault, according to the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office.

He also faces several aggravating circumstances, "including that the crime involved great violence, the victim was particularly vulnerable, the manner in which the crime was carried out indicated planning, sophistication or professionalism, and that Brambles engaged in violent conduct indicating a serious danger to society," the district attorney’s office said.

CALIFORNIA SUED OVER POLICY THAT COULD FREE SERIAL KILLERS AS LACI PETERSON'S FRIEND SOUNDS ALARM

Michael Douglas Brambles, 77, is charged with kidnapping to commit robbery while personally using a firearm in connection with an alleged robbery and sexual assault, according to the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office. (Ventura County District Attorney's Office; Lou Benoist/ AFP via Getty Images)

Brambles allegedly entered Arabella’s Boutique in Thousand Oaks, California, when a woman identified as SW was closing, pointed a handgun at her, and forced her into the backroom where he tied her hands behind her back and sexually assaulted her.

He is also accused of stealing from the business before he left.

The sexual assault allegations cannot be charged because the statute of limitations has passed.

Shortly after the crime, Brambles was identified as a suspect, but he was already being prosecuted for a string of robberies and sexual assaults.

He was convicted on 26 counts, including 18 armed robberies and multiple sexual assaults.

After being sentenced to 102 years, SW’s case was dismissed, which she agreed with, believing he would spend the rest of his life in prison.

But he was able to apply for parole in 2020 under a California law that allows elderly inmates to apply.

NEWSOM-BACKED LAW LETS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHILD RAPIST SEEK EARLY RELEASE AGAIN AS DA URGES 'STOP THE MADNESS'

Victim SW speaks at the Ventura County District Attorney's Office press conference this week. (Ventura County District Attorney's Office)

At his parole hearing, Brambles denied sexually assaulting any women besides the cases he had already been convicted for in Los Angeles County.

While examining SW’s cold case as part of the federal Sexual Assault Kit Initiative, Ventura County District Attorney’s Office investigators realized he had been paroled.

Brambles was arrested on Wednesday and is being held in Ventura County on $2 million bail.

"A few months ago, when investigators from the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office contacted me, I was shocked to hear not only that this man was walking free, but that he had been out of prison for six years," SW said at a press conference this week. "The justice that I and his other victims deserved was denied when he was only required to serve a fraction of the sentence he earned. I am thankful to have this opportunity now to seek justice for myself and for his other victims."

HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER

The Ventura County District Attorney's office in California. (Ventura County District Attorny's Office/Facebook)

Brambles faces a maximum sentence of 12 years to life if convicted.

"Without her courage, bravery and resolve to once again face the person who allegedly attacked her, we would not be here today," District Attorney Erik Nasarenko said of SW at the press conference. "Despite the passage of time and the long road ahead, SW is committed to seeing Michael Brambles held responsible for these violent accusations from 32 years ago, and so are we."

Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Why is the latest Ebola outbreak worsening?
articles.excerpt:

The Ebola outbreak in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has already killed 2,000 people.

It is spreading faster than any previous ...
articles.body_text:
Virus spreading in DRC faster than containment efforts.

The Ebola outbreak in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has already killed 2,000 people.

It is spreading faster than any previous outbreak, outpacing efforts to contain it, says the World Health Organization (WHO).

articles.title: Rescuers search for survivors of powerful Indonesia earthquake
articles.excerpt:
Watch: Buildings partially collapse in Indonesia after 7.7 earthquake

Rescue teams in Indonesia have been searching for survivors of Saturday's major earthquake which left at least 47 people dead.

T...
articles.body_text:
Watch: Buildings partially collapse in Indonesia after 7.7 earthquake

Rescue teams in Indonesia have been searching for survivors of Saturday's major earthquake which left at least 47 people dead.

The magnitude 7.7 quake struck the island of Flores shortly before 05:00 (22:00 GMT on Friday) and had a depth of 15km, Indonesia's meteorology and geophysics agency stated.

Preliminary reports indicate hundreds of buildings have been severely damaged by the quake and the dozens of aftershocks that followed.

However, the full scale of the disaster is still unclear, and news of a second earthquake of magnitude 6.9 at the other end of Indonesia served as a reminder of why they call this region the ring of fire.

Tremors from Saturday's powerful earthquake were reportedly felt by residents as far west as Bima Regency and City, the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) agency said, but the Manggarai province is among the most affected.

Preliminary data shows that 24 fatalities had been recorded there, meanwhile 17 deaths were recorded in East Manggarai province, three in Sikka province, and at least one in each of the Ngada, Ende and West Manggarai provinces.

At least two others had been seriously injured and 11 slightly injured.

The BNPB said aid was being sent to the affected areas with 10,500 packages arriving at the base operations so far.

It will take time to assess the full extent of the destruction in the region, which is remote and mountainous.

The area is mountainous and the assessment will take time, officials say

However, early reports indicate more than 150 houses had been severely damaged, as well as dozens of educational institutions, a number of healthcare facilities, places of worship, offices, and several other public facilities.

Video taken at the port in Maumere - the largest town in Flores - showed large chunks of concrete breaking off the terminal building onto passengers waiting to board an inter-island ferry. Some were thrown into the sea when the gangway to a ship collapsed.

Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena, governor of East Nusa Tenggara province, told a news conference that they were killed in their sleep by collapsing rubble.

Others, like Arnold Welianto, who lives in Talibura, a village near the coastline in Sikka, East Nusa Tenggara, were shaken out of their beds.

"I was startled awake and immediately went to my child's room." He said.

He also told the BBC that many people had already fled into the hills because the sea had also receded.

The earthquake struck around 600 miles (1,000km) away from Bali

Rescue teams worked tirelessly through the day to free those trapped under the rubble

While a tsunami warning was initially issued - leading some 2,000 people to self-evacuate - it was lifted around three hours after the initial jolt, when no significant sea level rise was detected.

Landslides, however, did block access to some villages but the experienced rescue teams worked tirelessly through the day to free those trapped under the rubble.

In Ruteng, a temporary medical tent was also assembled outside of a hospital to treat earthquake victims.

People could be seen moving inland after authorities issued a tsunami warning, which was later lifted

The ongoing advice from BNPB is for people to remain calm and to stay away from coastal areas and structures showing signs of damage.

Indonesia is prone to earthquakes and volcanic activity, lying along the meeting point of three major tectonic plates.

The ...
articles.body_text:
Kevin Wildes, Nick Wright, Chris Broussard and Eric Mangini discuss whether Jayden Daniels is overreacting to the number controversy and if the Steelers could move on from Aaron Rodgers in 2026.

The regular season hasn’t started yet, but Jayden Daniels is already being blitzed.

The New York Mets joined the masses on the internet who have made fun of the Washington Commanders star quarterback for sending a cease-and-desist letter earlier this month to his alma mater, LSU, over the use of his name, image and likeness.

After the Mets’ 4-1 win over the Washington Nationals, who, like the Commanders, are in the DMV area, the Mets took a shot at Daniels on X.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) passes against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of an NFL wild-card playoff football game in Tampa, Fla., Sunday, Jan. 12, 2025. (AP Photo/Jason Behnken)

"Stopped at 4 out of respect for Jayden Daniels," the Mets wrote in the viral post.

Daniels, who won the Heisman Trophy with LSU in 2023, and his camp reportedly felt that head coach Lane Kiffin allowing DJ Pickett to wear his No. 5 jersey was "disrespectful." The former LSU star quarterback posted a statement on social media Thursday afternoon about the situation.

"I have been locked in on training camp and that's been my number one focus. I have a lot of gratitude for my time at LSU and I'm proud of what my teammates and I accomplished there," Daniels posted. "Obviously there are issues to be worked out between my team and LSU and my hope is that it will get done privately."

JAYDEN DANIELS TELLS LSU TO KEEP HIS NAME OUT OF ITS MOUTH IN WILD NO. 5 JERSEY FEUD INVOLVING NIL

Jayden Daniels No. 5 of the LSU Tigers warms up before facing the Alabama Crimson Tide at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Ala., on Nov. 4, 2023. (Getty Images)

"My sole personal focus is on Commanders' football. I realize the business of football is unique and I trust this can all be resolved."

While Daniels tried to quell the situation, social media has only come after him as hard as any pass rush he will face this season.

StubHub, a ticketing website, said in a post on X that it will no longer offer tickets in groups of five out of respect for Daniels.

The former LSU star can only hope that by the time the regular season begins, the only blitz he is facing is on the field and not online.

Follow Fox News Digital’s sports coverage on X, and subscribe to the Fox News Sports Huddle newsletter.

Ryan Canfield is a digital production assistant for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Australian state to launch gun buyback after Bondi Beach attack
articles.excerpt:
Mourners placed tributes after 15 people were murdered near Bondi Beach

Australia's most populous state will launch a gun buyback scheme later this year, becoming the first to offer cash in exchange ...
articles.body_text:
Mourners placed tributes after 15 people were murdered near Bondi Beach

Australia's most populous state will launch a gun buyback scheme later this year, becoming the first to offer cash in exchange for firearms in the wake of the Bondi Beach terror attack.

Gun owners in New South Wales (NSW) will be offered up to AUS$1,000 (£523) to hand over eligible handguns, shotguns and rifles from 2 November.

Australian authorities had pledged sweeping firearm law reforms after 15 people were shot dead at a Jewish festival on Sydney's Bondi Beach, which is located in NSW, last December.

The state's premier Chris Minns said on Saturday: "We want those guns handed in, compensated for and safely destroyed."

He said the move could see hundreds of thousands of guns surrendered.

Gun ownership reforms already introduced by the state mean individuals can only own four firearms - although some people, such as farmers and sports shooters, can own a maximum of 10.

The scheme will be offered to those who have more weapons than permitted by the new rules, or who are no longer covered by a licence - with terms having been reduced from five years to two.

The scheme will be implemented in two phases. The first - from the start of November - covers types of handguns, shotguns and rifles.

Those handing over a revolver, for example, will be paid AUS$1,000, while an air rifle will fetch AUS$450.

The second phase will begin early next year and cover "higher-value firearms" valued above AUS$3,000, capped at AUS$10,000.

The National Gun BuyBack Scheme is being jointly funded by New South Wales and the federal government.

Businesses will be able to receive up to AUS$25,000 in support to help them adjust to the reforms, with help also offered to gun-dealers.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said: "We must do everything we can to make sure the antisemitic terrorist attack in Bondi doesn't happen again.

"That includes meaningful nationwide gun reform."

On 14 December last year, 15 people including a 10-year-old girl and a Holocaust survivor were killed as Hanukkah celebrations took place near Australia's most famous beach.

Australian authorities had initially planned a nationwide gun buyback, though plans have been delayed over funding and how it would be implemented.

articles.title: Indiana Pacers' star Tyrese Haliburton has one major problem with the new NBA schedule
articles.excerpt: The WNBA’s official "task force" met to answer a basic question—what is a woman?—on the heels of Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham taking a stand to protect women's sports and former NBA players En...
articles.body_text:
The WNBA’s official "task force" met to answer a basic question—what is a woman?—on the heels of Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham taking a stand to protect women's sports and former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White declaring for the 2027 WNBA Draft. After failing to reach a conclusion, Commissioner Cathy Engelbert’s league blamed outside "hate and vitriol" and simply scheduled more meetings. On this episode of Don't @ Me, Dan Dakich breaks down the absolute clown show as the WNBA continues to get in its own way.

The NBA schedule was rolled out this week, and not everyone was happy with how it looked.

One of those people? Indiana Pacers' star Tyrese Haliburton.

It's kind of hard to believe, but the last time we saw Haliburton in action was in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, when he tore the Achilles tendon in his right leg, and the Pacers lost to the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Tyrese Haliburton missed all of last season due to an injury suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. ((Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images))

That injury forced the former Iowa State Cyclone — who was one of the biggest stars of those playoffs — to sit out the entire 2025-26 season, but now he's ready for action.

On the road... in New Orleans... and not on national TV.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Name any other person that you compare to my level of a basketball player, wherever you have me ranked. If they tore their Achilles and missed 16 months, do you think that game would be on national television?" Haliburton asked on the "Number on the Board" podcast.

MIKE BREEN SAYS FANS 'DESERVE TO BE THROWN A BONE' AS NBA CUTS ALL LOCAL BROADCASTS FROM THE PLAYOFFS

"Do you think that game would be at home, if not on national television?" he continued. "Do you think that that game would be at New Orleans?"

Tyrese Haliburton was not happy that his return to the Pacers lineup will happen on the road against the New Orleans Pelicans. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images)

Alright, for starters, Tyrese, prepare to get booed in New Orleans...

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

It's hard to make everyone happy when scheduling 82 games for each of the league's 30 teams, but the highly anticipated return of a player who missed an entire season after being one of the big stories the season before seems like it should be a priority.

Obviously, the league's priorities are elsewhere. There's a reason LeBron and the 76ers will head to Madison Square Garden to face the defending champion Knicks on the first night of the season.

It might seem a bit much, but I can get why Haliburton feels that he and the Pacers may have been slighted on this one.

A Florida middle school teacher was arrested after investigators said he exchanged inappropriate messages with a forme...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Florida middle school teacher was arrested after investigators said he exchanged inappropriate messages with a former teenage student and acknowledged communicating inappropriately with the student since 2023.

Christian Schneider, 31, a teacher at Memorial Middle School, was arrested Friday on charges of three felonies following an investigation by the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office.

Detectives opened a criminal investigation into Schneider on July 28, and learned he had been sending inappropriate messages to a former teenage student at Franklin Middle School, according to the sheriff's office.

KENTUCKY MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER ACCUSED OF CROSSING THE LINE WITH STUDENT, ARRESTED UNDER NEW ANTI-GROOMING LAW

Christian Schneider, 31, a teacher at Memorial Middle School, was arrested on Aug. 14, 2026, on three felony charges, according to the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office. (Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office)

Schneider told deputies he had engaged in inappropriate communication with the student since 2023, authorities said.

Authorities have not disclosed the student's exact age, how investigators learned about the alleged communications or further details about the messages.

Schneider faces two counts of solicitation or possession of child sexual abuse material, both second-degree felonies, according to Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office booking records.

He also faces one count of unlawful use of a two-way communications device, a third-degree felony.

HIGH SCHOOL COUNSELOR PLEADS GUILTY TO MULTIPLE SEX CRIMES INVOLVING TEEN SHE WAS MEANT TO HELP

The Hillsborough County Sheriff's office said the investigation remains active. (Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office)

The booking records list July 3 as the offense date for each of the three charges.

Schneider was arrested shortly after noon Friday and booked into custody that afternoon, according to jail records.

Each charge carried a $2,500 surety bond, for a combined $7,500. Schneider was released on surety bond at 2:38 a.m. local time Saturday, jail records show.

"Teachers hold a position of trust that comes with enormous responsibility," said Sheriff Chad Chronister. "When that trust is exploited, it's not just a crime, it's a violation of everything our schools are supposed to stand for. Detectives will continue investigating these cases aggressively, and anyone who abuses their position with a child will be held accountable."

The sheriff's office identified Schneider as a teacher at Memorial Middle School and the teenager as his former student at Franklin Middle School.

Memorial Middle School in Tampa, Florida, where Christian Schneider worked as a teacher at the time of his arrest, according to the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office. (Google Maps)

The agency did not provide additional details about Schneider's connection to Franklin Middle School or when he taught the student.

The sheriff's office said the investigation remains active and that additional information will be released as it becomes available.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Hillsborough County school district for information about Schneider's employment status and for comment on his arrest.

Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

articles.title: Michael Penix Jr and Tua Tagovailoa have already given us a potential 'Meme of the Year' contender

The NFL preseaso...
articles.body_text:
Jason Hammer and Dan Zaksheske join Dan Dakich for this week's edition of Shot Clock Violation featuring Stephanie White's meltdown, LA Lakers sale, the death of woke ESPN, and more!

The NFL preseason is barely underway, and it didn't take long to be gifted what sure looks like the premier meme of the 2026 season.

And we have Michael Penix Jr. to thank for it.

The Atlanta Falcons hosted the Denver Broncos on Friday to get their preseason slate rolling, and there was a moment on the sidelines that has been getting all the attention.

DRAKE LONDON SIGNS $141M DEAL WITH FALCONS, BECOMING THIRD HIGHEST-PAID RECEIVER IN NFL: REPORTS

Falcons quarterbacks Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. gave fans what looks destined to be an all-time meme early in the preseason. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images)

Tua Tagovailoa — who the team acquired over the offseason — was sitting on the bench after his first possession in a Falcons uniform.

That's when Penix, who was standing nearby, pointed at him and made a bewildered face.

I would be willing to bet there's another explanation for why Penix was pointing and doing the "Can you believe this?" face that everyone did on "The Office."

RAIDERS ROOKIE FERNANDO MENDOZA THANKS GOD FOR AN NFL DEBUT THAT COMPARES FAVORABLY TO 'MR BRADY'

But it doesn't matter why he did it. All that matters is he did it, and it's about to be the meme of the year.

The NFL is always a fertile ground for memery.

Hell, by the time the regular season gets underway, I think there's a good chance this meme is old news and something else will take its place.

Michael Penix Jr. is still battling back from injury, with Tua Tagovailoa joining the team's quarterback room this season. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images)

Penix — believed to be the Falcons' starter — did not see any action in the game as he is still working his way back from an injury. Meanwhile, Tagovailoa completed three of his five passing attempts for 22 yards.

The rest of the snaps went to Jack Strand and Cooper Rush. Strand completed half of his 12 pass attempts for 50 yards and a touchdown, while Rush had a nightmare 7-for-19 night with 62 yards and a pair of interceptions in the Dirty Birds' 27-7 loss.
